changes: Light theme: Settings → Appearance now offers Dark, Light and Match system. Terminals, notes, reviews and the window frame change with it, and status colours keep their meaning in both. Switch from the command palette too (Toggle light / dark theme).
Interface size: make the whole window 90%, 110% or 125% in Settings → Appearance. Terminal text keeps its own font size on top.
Command palette: the letters you typed are marked in each result, the commands you ran last come first, and a footer shows the keys.
Smoother: menus and the palette open with a short fade, buttons respond when pressed, and the window cross-fades when the theme changes. Turn on reduced motion in your OS and all of that stays still.
Open folder and Browse… start in the project you have open, or in your home folder when none is, instead of wherever the system dialog was last (often Downloads).

Diagrams: a code map of the imports between your folders (TypeScript and JavaScript, tsconfig paths included) and a database diagram of the tables and foreign keys in Prisma schemas and SQL migrations. Parsed on your machine; open it from the Explorer header or the command palette, double-click a box to open it in your editor, and copy either one as Mermaid.
Recipes: a new section to see, build and share factory recipes. Open it from the Factory sidebar, the start screen or the command palette.

Recipe builder: name it, start from a template or an existing recipe, add agent, check and pull request stages, and save. No YAML to write; placeholders like {spec.out} are one click, and it tells you what's missing before you save.

Share recipes: copy one as text, export it to a file, and import from a paste, the clipboard or a file. The import shows what it adds first, keeps your own agents, and never adds the same recipe twice.
A recipe stage with just a prompt runs on your default agent.
New factory run: what to build comes right after the recipe; per-stage agents and the start point fold away until you need them.
The Factory sidebar lists your recipes, with a run button on each.
Start screen: a Software Factory card with New run and Recipes.
Overview: "need you" now counts factory runs waiting for your approval, and factory runs show their status and recipe.

Repeat: run the same mission pass after pass, each building on the last. Set how many passes, the minutes between them and an optional check command (Factory → Automations → Repeat, or Repeat… on a mission or agent task). Unattended passes run in print mode and end when the agent exits; interactive ones end when you click Accept pass. Every pass is committed in the loop's worktree, the next one gets the last report and a failed check's output, and the loop stops when a pass changes nothing or the check fails twice.
CLI: sldev new --repeat 5 --gap 30m --check "npm test" runs the same loop from the terminal; --print runs a single agent that exits when done; sldev accept and sldev loops.
CLI on Windows: install it with npm like on Linux and macOS. The background daemon, git and helper processes no longer flash console windows, and notifications are Windows toasts.

CLI: Ctrl-b w shows the repository's GitHub Actions runs (rerun failed jobs, open one in the browser), Ctrl-b e opens the pane's folder in your editor and Ctrl-b v its changed files side by side. sldev open, sldev workflows and sldev clean (finished panes and their worktrees, asked first) do the same from the command line.

New mission form: the agent and profile come first, other agents to compare are one-click chips, and the folder, branch and model fold into one Options line that says what will happen. The whole form fits without scrolling.
Mission cards say the next step: Answer when the agent waits for you, Review 3 files when it's done, Build from this after a research or plan mission.
Start screen: type what an agent should do and press Enter to open the New mission form with it. With a project open, the agent card comes first.
Settings has jump links to its sections.
Factory graphs shrink to fit the panel before they scroll, and stage cards no longer squash the agent name.
Fix: a multi-line prompt echoed in the terminal drew as a staircase. Long prompts now show their first lines; the whole brief is in the mission details.
Fix: the Overview counted a mission started a moment ago only after up to 30 seconds.

Fix: Codex missions and factory stages failed to start with Codex 0.16x, which dropped the --full-auto flag. Workspace-write mode now uses --sandbox workspace-write, which old and new versions accept.
Save for later: write a mission now and launch it when you're ready. Saved missions sit under "Saved for later" in the Agents tab and Mission Control, and you can edit them before launching.

Review changes opens in a tab of its own: side by side or unified, a file list with folders, Viewed to fold a file away, and the acceptance criteria on top. The sidebars step aside while you review (Settings → Editor).
Diff in your editor: with VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf or a JetBrains IDE, open a file's changes in the editor's own diff view from the review.
Focus mode (Ctrl+Alt+F, Cmd+Alt+F on a Mac) hides both sidebars, and split panes have a maximize button.
Factory runs open their stage terminals below the pipeline instead of beside it, so the graph keeps its width.
Fix: the usage dashboard showed an empty grey block next to its tiles.

Mission kinds: Build, Research, Investigate, Plan, Review, Map project and Freeform. Each frames your brief for the job; Research and Review run in the agent's read-only mode, and Freeform sends your prompt exactly as written. Your own kinds are Markdown templates in .sldev/missions.
Build from this: a finished Research or Plan mission becomes the brief of a Build mission or the start of a factory run.

Continue on another agent: when Claude Code, Codex or another agent stops at its plan's usage limit, the next agent in your order picks up the work in the same folder (Settings → Agents). Factory stages can do it on their own.
Software Factory: run your own spec, build and review skills as stages (skill: in a recipe), swap the agent or skill of any stage for one run, and start a run from a spec you already have.
Automations: start a recipe or a mission on a schedule, when CI fails on a branch, or when an issue gets a label. They run while the app is open and never push.

Project context: what agents learn goes into .sldev/memory.md and a local index linked to your code. Missions are pointed at the notes that match their brief, and the Context tab lets you browse, search and pin them.
Mission Control: missions, factory runs and usage in one tab, as status columns, a grid or a list.
Needs you for every agent: approval prompts on screen now count, not only the terminal bell, so OpenCode, Codex and Gemini dialogs show up. Mission details say how each agent's status is known.
Agents that don't report back get their final screen as the mission's report.
Fix: a Claude Code reply written just after it finished could be lost, leaving the report empty and Build from this disabled. Missions that lost it get it back on the next start.
Tab layout: keep open terminals as tabs on top, or list them down the left side of each group (Settings → Terminal → Tab layout, or "Toggle tab layout" in the command palette).
Fix: the resize cursor (↔) could stay stuck everywhere after dragging a sidebar edge if the window lost focus mid-drag.
Fix: GitHub Workflows showed "Unexpected end of JSON input" for a repository without Actions. It now says the repository has no workflows yet.
A right sidebar with Overview, Agents, Skills and Workflows tabs. Overview shows what needs you, today's usage and the latest missions. Hide it to a slim icon rail (Ctrl+Alt+Shift+B, ⌘⌥B on Mac).

Copy from terminals: right-click for Copy, Paste, Select all and Copy all output. Ctrl+C copies when text is selected, and Ctrl+V pastes on Windows. In agent screens, hold Shift while dragging to select (Option on Mac).
Fix: Cursor missions failed on Windows. Cursor now starts as "agent" (or "cursor-agent" on older installs), and prompts arrive whole.
Fix: on Windows, a task that runs a .ps1 script opened it in Notepad. It now runs in PowerShell.

Fix: the app could freeze for a while, mostly on Windows. Token usage is now read incrementally, and tool lookups no longer block the app. If it still happens, About → Copy diagnostics lists each freeze.
GitHub Workflows splits into Workflows and Runs sections that scroll on their own, and workflow logs open on Windows too.
New shell tasks offer the scripts in their folder (package.json, Makefile, justfile, …) to pick from.
What's new: after an update, sldev-io shows what changed (also under Help → What's new, and on the website's changelog).
Report a bug or send an idea from the app: it opens a GitHub issue with your versions already filled in.
The taskbar and dock icon shows how many missions need you.
Optional sound when a mission needs you (Settings → General).
Fix: on Windows, agents received only part of the prompt (sometimes a single word). Agents now start without a shell, and every prompt arrives whole, with its line breaks, quotes and symbols.
Removing a mission asks first, says what is removed and kept, and never throws away uncommitted work unless you tick it. The same goes for every other delete.
Missions take acceptance criteria, keep the agent's final report, and take your handoff notes. Follow-up and Second opinion pass both on to the next agent.
Agents dashboard: every running agent with what it's doing, how long it has run and its tokens. Ctrl+Shift+J jumps to the next one that needs you.
Software Factory: recipes run agents and checks as a pipeline, with bake-offs, PR feedback and run history.
Agent profiles, rules sync to every agent's instruction file, and a usage dashboard with a timeline and estimated cost.
Missions, factory runs, skills and tasks can work in any folder: type a path, Browse…, or pick a recent one.
A new look: one colour per status everywhere, counts on the sidebar icons, start cards in the empty dock, Ping and Save & Connect for SSH hosts.
The version is shown in the title bar; click it to open Settings → About.
The terminal installer always installs the version from the website, even over a local build.
Automatic updates on Windows and Linux; on macOS the app tells you when a new version is out.
Settings → About with versions, diagnostics to copy and links to the legal pages.
The Linux build runs on older distributions (glibc 2.35 and newer).
Installers are published to the public downloads page.
The free beta runs until the date on the website.
First beta: terminals, runtimes and tasks, agent missions for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor Agent, GitHub Copilot, OpenCode, Gemini CLI and custom CLIs.
Skills, workflows, notes, SSH with a credential vault, Docker containers and a first-run setup check.
